doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Return to New York in the late 1960s
title: Clifford Jordan's New Frontier dates with Don Cherry and Ed Blackwell
summary: Jordan arranges four rotating-leader dates; they were never released.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, anyway, we played the job. Right after that, Blue say, "Well, I'm going into Minton's --" Minton's was still open -- "for a week. Wilbur, you want to make it?" I said, "Sure." Well, before this happened, I get a call from Clifford Jordan. Clifford and a friend of his, Harvey Brown, had formed a record company called New Frontier Records. He called me up, say, "Wilbur, look, I got four dates for you. Four paying dates. You get paid the same day that you make the records." I said, "Yeah, that's it." He says, "Well, the first day, see, is my date, and I'm using Don Cherry, Eddie Blackwell and you. The next day, it'll be Don Cherry's date as leader," same personnel.
"And the next date, it'll be Eddie Blackwell's date, with the same personnel, only he'll be the leader. The next date will be your date, same personnel."

See, each one of us will be a leader and a side man on the other three dates, you know, other three days, which was a little taste of nice and I could take the money for four days' work. We was recording this down at a loft down on Grand Street, Dennis
Charles is the drummer, used to work with Cecil Taylor and Steve Lacey (PHONETIC) and Billy Higgins was on part of that date, too, along with Eddie Blackwell.

Anyway, we made that date and those dates at least and as yet, they have never been released. But that wasn't the only dates that Clifford and Harvey put up. We made some more. I'll get to that a little later.
